textRefs.debunk_axis3: Y 轴起点是 90%——柱子之间的差异被夸大了，让人以为满意度和「近乎完美」只有一步之遥；真实起点 0 时差距就没那么体面了。
textRefs.debunk_avg: 这根柱是「已流失客户」的满意度（15%）——它被拉低，是因为流失的人根本不在抽样里！把他们的真实感受算进来，「99% 满意度」就站不住了。

zh.explanation: 这张满意度图有两个陷阱：①Y 轴从 90% 起，把各组的微小差距放大成「都很满意」的假象；②「已流失客户」只有 15% 满意度，说明抽样根本没覆盖不活跃用户——把流失的人算进去，整体满意度会大打折扣。看满意度数据先问：问了谁？没问谁？

en.chartTitle: Customer Satisfaction as High as 99%? Unit: %

textRefs.debunk_axis3: The Y axis starts at 90% — the gaps between bars are exaggerated, making everything look one step from "near perfect"; from an honest baseline of 0 the differences are far less flattering.
textRefs.debunk_avg: This bar is churned customers' satisfaction (15%) — it is dragged down because churned users were never in the sample! Count their true feelings and the "99% satisfaction" collapses.

manual: Check whether the Y axis starts at 0
Does the average hide extremes or people who were never surveyed?
hints: With the Y axis starting at 90%, "nearly perfect" is an illusion
The churned customers' low bar exposes the sampling hole
en.explanation: This satisfaction chart hides two traps: ① the Y axis starts at 90%, inflating tiny gaps into the illusion that everyone is happy; ② "churned customers" score only 15%, showing the survey never covered inactive users — include the leavers and overall satisfaction collapses. When reading satisfaction data, ask: who was asked? who was not?
